title: Cre-dependent viral payloads: DIO and fDIO
objective: Explain how DIO/FLEX makes a viral payload Cre-dependent, and how combining it with a Cre line adds a cell-type switch to viral delivery.

steps.title: Make the virus obey Cre
steps.body: You can build a viral payload that's **off until [[Cre]] acts** — just like a bred-in [[loxP|floxed]]-STOP, but delivered by [[AAV]]. The common design is **[[DIO]]** (a.k.a. **FLEX**): the payload is inverted and flanked by loxP sites, so **Cre flips it into the correct orientation** to be expressed. No Cre in that cell → it stays inverted → silent.

visual.alt: Three filters — retrograde route, DIO switch, and a subtype Cre line — narrow a mixed population down to the single target neuron.
visual.caption: Each layer of specificity removes off-target cells, leaving your target.

steps.title: Two switches, two recombinases
steps.body:
- **AAV-DIO-<payload>** → turns on only in **Cre+** cells.
- **AAV-fDIO-<payload>** → the [[Flp]] version, on only in **Flp+** cells.

So you can bring the same [[intersectional genetics|intersectional]] logic from C3 into viral delivery: a DIO virus in a cell-type Cre line expresses only where the virus went AND the cell is Cre+.

visual.alt: Interactive: choose route (retrograde vs local), payload switch (non-conditional vs DIO), and mouse line, then see which cell populations express the DREADD.
visual.caption: Compose route + switch + Cre line — see which cells get the DREADD.

steps.prompt: You inject AAV-DIO-[[hM3Dq]] broadly, but into a TrkB-Cre mouse. Where does the [[DREADD]] express?
options: Every single cell that the virus managed to enter
Only the TrkB-Cre+ cells that the virus also entered
Only the non-neuronal cells around the injection site
Nowhere, because DIO blocks all expression entirely
steps.explanation: DIO needs Cre to flip it on. So expression = (virus got in) AND (cell is Cre+). The Cre line adds cell-type specificity to the spatial specificity of the injection.

variants.setup: You inject AAV-DIO-hM3Dq broadly into a TrkB-Cre mouse.
options: Every single cell that the virus managed to enter
Only the TrkB-Cre+ cells that the virus also entered
Only the non-neuronal cells around the injection site
Nowhere, because DIO blocks all expression entirely
variants.reveal: DIO payloads need Cre to flip on, so expression is the intersection of 'virus reached it' and 'Cre+.'

steps.prompt: Match each tool to its 'on' condition.
pairs: On in Cre+ cells the virus entered
On in Flp+ cells the virus entered
Delivers Cre to cells projecting to the injection site
On in any cell the virus entered (with the promoter)
steps.explanation: Mixing these — e.g. [[retrograde]] Cre from the organ + a DIO-DREADD in the [[DRG]] — is how you compose precise access.

steps.setup: Plan: AAV2-retro-Cre injected into the pancreas + AAV-DIO-[[hM4Di]] injected into (or expressed in) the DRG.
steps.prompt: Which neurons end up with the silencing DREADD?
options: All DRG neurons, regardless of where their axons project
DRG neurons projecting to pancreas that also received the DIO virus
Only the pancreatic acinar cells right near the injection
None at all; this two-part system cannot express anything
steps.reveal: Retrograde Cre marks the pancreas-projecting neurons; the DIO-hM4Di turns on only where Cre is present. The intersection = pancreas-projecting DRG neurons carrying the DREADD. This is a clean, composable targeting strategy for your project.

variants.prompt: Retrograde Cre from the pancreas plus a DIO silencing-DREADD AAV. Which neurons end up with the silencing DREADD?
options: All DRG neurons, regardless of where their axons project
DRG neurons projecting to pancreas that also received the DIO virus
Only the pancreatic acinar cells right near the injection
None at all; this two-part system cannot express anything
variants.explanation: Two requirements intersect: retrograde Cre (projects to pancreas) and the DIO virus being present.
